Experience working in an academic medical setting.

The UCI Brunson Center for Translational Vision Research (BCTVR) is seeking a detail-oriented and analytical Research Administrator to join our administrative team. Under the general direction of the Associate Research Director, the Research Administrator will play a critical role in managing financial aspects of research grants, ensuring compliance, and supporting faculty with research administration.
Key Responsibilities Include:

Grant and Financial Management: Oversee post-award financial administration of research grants, including budget preparation, financial reporting, reconciliations, and cost accounting. Ensure compliance with NIH and institutional policies.

Payroll and Salary Management: Maintain salary worksheets, process payroll distributions, and track personnel effort on grants to ensure accurate funding allocations. Financial Reporting and Reconciliation: Prepare and reconcile financial reports, track expenditures, analyze budget variances, and provide recommendations to optimize resource utilization.

Reimbursement Management: Process and monitor travel, purchasing, and reimbursement requests for faculty, staff, trainees, and visiting scholars. Review documentation for accuracy and compliance with university and sponsor policies, track reimbursement status, and resolve issues to ensure timely payment.
Fund Accounting & Compliance: Manage fund allocations and cost accounting to ensure proper usage of grant funds. Monitor adherence to university policies and sponsor guidelines.
Collaboration & Problem-Solving: Work in a dynamic team environment, demonstrating effective problem-solving skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities efficiently.
This role requires strong organizational and analytical skills, attention to detail, and the ability to navigate complex financial and administrative systems in a research setting.
Working knowledge of finance policies, practices, and systems.
Intermediate knowledge and understanding of internal control practices and their impact on protecting University resources.
Ability to gather reasonably retrievable information to organize and perform financial analysis assignments.
Demonstrated ability to effectively present information verbally and in writing clearly and concisely.
Demonstrated ability using spreadsheet and database software, specifically Microsoft Office Suite for financial analysis, fiscal management, and financial reports.

Demonstrated interpersonal skills at all levels within the unit; excellent service orientation and critical thinking skills; and attention to detail. Demonstrated ability using organizational skills to multi-task in a high-volume environment.
Demonstrated ability to respond with flexibility and efficiency to frequent changes in task focus, competing priorities, and multiple and sometimes competing deadlines.
Ability to work well with others, in both one-on-one capacity and in group settings.
Strong computer skills using MS Office Suite, Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.
